Subject: Dedicated reservation: ramp staircase + triggered activation windows (NovaOptic)

Hi Elena / Tomas —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a compact proposal that lays out three reservation pathways tailored to NovaOptic's expected LLM throughput for the next 12 months. High-level summary here so you can forward to procurement: 

- Option A (Conservative): 12 GPUs reserved (N1-class), 2-week canary, warmup credits = 50k tokens. Ideal if you want low upfront cost and stepwise scale.
- Option B (Balanced): 24 GPUs reserved (mix H100/Arm H-series nodes), min activation 16 GPUs after month 1, 3-month staircase ramp to 48 GPUs. Recommended for steady growth with cost predictability.
- Option C (Throughput-first): 48 GPUs reserved, immediate 32-GPU min active, includes burst lanes. For production at launch with strict latency SLOs.

Key controls in the proposal:
- Minimum active GPU policy (you only pay for the reserved commitment but we guarantee a minimum active allocation to meet latency targets).
- Triggered activations: automated scale steps based on 7-day rolling utilization or SLA breaches — e.g., if 7-day avg > 65% for 72 hours, auto-activate next ramp tranche.
- Canary & warmup: 2-week canary on first tranche, followed by staged warmup credits to pre-populate caches (prefix caching) and avoid cold-start latency.

I've included a sample activation cadence (sheet attached) and a short SLA excerpt showing 99.95% uptime for Dedicated lanes. Ben will follow up on the kernel/quantization profile recommendations for your model family.

Next steps I propose: 1) You pick A/B/C or suggest a hybrid, 2) procurement sends redlines, 3) we lock schedule + first invoice milestone (typically activation).

Attachments: 20261201-novaoptic-reservation-proposal.xlsx; sla-sample-2026.pdf

Thanks,
Diego

Hi Elena — quick answers inline, and a couple of operational notes.

1) Billing model: Reserved capacity is a committed monthly charge. Activation (turning more GPUs active) does not change the committed charge; it changes how we allocate capacity within your pool. For burst beyond reserved capacity we bill on usage rates. If you choose a lower active floor than the reserved commit, you still pay the commitment; we can, however, structure an "activation credit" that refunds a portion of the commitment for underutilization in the first 60 days (common for pilots).

2) Warmup credits: These are token credits applied to the first N tokens processed by the Dedicated pool during the warmup window. They do not roll forward beyond the 90-day expiry window in the sheet, but we can negotiate carry-forward for enterprise agreements.

3) Region: yes — Dedicated lanes are provisioned in us-west-2 as a standard option. Burst lanes can be region-local or routed cross-region with a fallback. We'll mark your primary region as us-west-2 in the proposal.

Operational notes:
- Canary: 14-day canary for the first tranche with opt-in telemetry hooks for your engineers.
- Staircase triggers: we recommend 3 tranches over 12 weeks for Option B (16 -> 24 -> 36 GPUs active) with automated activation when 7-day avg utilization hits 60% for 48 hours.
- Minimums: we can offer a 30-day lookback usage credit worth up to 15% of the monthly commit if the average active utilization is below the agreed floor during onboarding.

I've updated the attached spreadsheet with the activation cadence and a sample invoice schedule (first invoice on activation of tranche 1, second invoice at tranche 2 activation or at 60 days).

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Thanks — noted. Quick replies and next steps so we stay on a tight path to signature: 

- SLA credits: we will include a financial credit ladder. Typical structure we propose: 10% credit for monthly uptime between 99.95% and 99.8%, 25% credit for 99.8%–99.5%, escalates beyond that. I'll have Legal produce the exact language but that's the commercial intent.
- Invoice cadence: we can accept net-45 for the initial tranche invoice (pilot activation). For longer-term reserved invoices we prefer net-30; we'll mark that in the SOW and note the first invoice milestone as activation of tranche 1.
- Data & audit exports: confirmed — audit logs and control-plane exports available on request in us-west-2; we'll include an access-runbook.
- DocuSign: Ben will prepare the SOW + Master Services Schedule and route it via DocuSign by EOD Thursday.

Immediate ask from NovaOptic: please confirm whether Option B (Balanced) with a 3-tranche 12-week staircase and a 16-GPU min active floor is acceptable. If yes, we'll move to SOW and schedule a 30-minute kickoff to align RTEs/Oncall and telemetry hooks.

Next steps checklist:
1) NovaOptic confirms Option B + 16 GPU minimum active floor.
2) Ben generates SOW + DocuSign (expected Thu).
3) Procurement confirms redline acceptance or flags anything odd (we will fast-track legal review).
4) Kickoff call scheduled within 3 business days of signature.
